events.title: Muhammad enters Mecca and clears the Kaaba of idols
events.description: By the usual reckoning, Muhammad and some 10,000 followers took Mecca with little bloodshed. The idols around the Kaaba were destroyed and it was rededicated as the centre of Islamic worship.
events.html: By the usual reckoning, Muhammad and some 10,000 followers took Mecca with little bloodshed. The idols around the Kaaba were destroyed and it was rededicated as the centre of Islamic worship.

events.title: The Qarmatians of Bahrayn sack Mecca during the Hajj
events.description: The Qarmatians of Bahrayn, an Isma'ili Shia militant movement centred in al-Ahsa in Eastern Arabia, sacked the Muslim holy city of Mecca amid the rituals of the Hajj. They had revolted against both the Fatimid and the Abbasid caliphates.

events.title: Theodora becomes sole ruler of the Byzantine Empire
events.description: Theodora Porphyrogenita, who had reigned as empress since 1042, became sole ruler of the Byzantine Empire until her death in August 1056. She was the last sovereign of the Macedonian dynasty, which had ruled the empire for almost 200 years.

events.title: Vladislaus II becomes King of Bohemia
events.description: Emperor Frederick Barbarossa granted Duke Vladislaus II a royal crown in return for support in Italy. He was crowned at Regensburg, only the second Bohemian ruler to hold the title of king.
events.html: Emperor Frederick Barbarossa granted Duke Vladislaus II a royal crown in return for support in Italy. He was crowned at Regensburg, only the second Bohemian ruler to hold the title of king.

events.title: England's first recorded state lottery is drawn
events.description: Chartered by Elizabeth I to raise money for harbours and public works, England's first state lottery was drawn at the west door of St Paul's Cathedral. Ticket holders were promised immunity from arrest for minor crimes.
events.html: Chartered by Elizabeth I to raise money for harbours and public works, England's first state lottery was drawn at the west door of St Paul's Cathedral. Ticket holders were promised immunity from arrest for minor crimes.

events.title: William Herschel discovers Titania and Oberon
events.description: Six years after finding Uranus, Herschel spotted its two largest moons. They were later named after the king and queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'.
events.html: Six years after finding Uranus, Herschel spotted its two largest moons. They were later named after the king and queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'.

events.title: Alabama secedes from the Union
events.description: Alabama's convention voted 61 to 39 to leave the United States, the fourth state to secede. Its capital Montgomery hosted the founding of the Confederate States the next month.
events.html: Alabama's convention voted 61 to 39 to leave the United States, the fourth state to secede. Its capital Montgomery hosted the founding of the Confederate States the next month.

events.title: Insulin is first given to a diabetic patient
events.description: Fourteen-year-old Leonard Thompson received an insulin extract at Toronto General Hospital. The first dose failed, but a purer extract made by James Collip saved his life later that month.
events.html: Fourteen-year-old Leonard Thompson received an insulin extract at Toronto General Hospital. The first dose failed, but a purer extract made by James Collip saved his life later that month.

events.title: Amelia Earhart sets out on the first solo flight from Hawaii
events.description: Earhart took off from Honolulu and landed in Oakland, California, about 18 hours later. She became the first person to fly solo across this stretch of the Pacific, some 3,900 km.
events.html: Earhart took off from Honolulu and landed in Oakland, California, about 18 hours later. She became the first person to fly solo across this stretch of the Pacific, some 3,900 km.

events.title: Albania proclaimed a People's Republic
events.description: Albania's assembly abolished the monarchy and declared a People's Republic under communist leader Enver Hoxha. His regime became one of the most isolated and repressive in Europe.

events.title: US Surgeon General reports that smoking causes cancer
events.description: Luther Terry's advisory committee concluded that cigarette smoking causes lung cancer in men. The report led to health warnings on cigarette packets and decades of anti-smoking policy.

song: A children's song from Okinawa, named after the balsam flower, that teaches children to honour what their parents tell them.
